subject: Schema Gate: Implementation Runway & Preflight Checklist
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@cardiotech.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Schema Gate: Implementation Runway & Preflight Checklist

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the demo last week. To make the enablement phase predictable for both teams, I put together a short "implementation runway" we typically run through when activating streaming + function/tool calling + structured outputs.

High level ask: can we align on owners, minimum acceptance criteria, and a proposed 3-week timeline before our pilot? If that works I’ll send a calendar invite for a 60-min kickoff.

Quick items I suggest we confirm in the kickoff:
- Schema gate: target JSON schema for structured outputs (example mapping + required fields)
- Tool / function contract: single RPC-style definition for calls, timeouts, and error semantics
- Streaming behavior: prefix caching rules, max latency SLOs under the pilot traffic profile
- Test harness: sample prompts, evaluation metric (P95 latency, token cost budget, and correctness checks)
- Security / network: egress IPs, certs, SOC2 evidence request cadence

I’m attaching a short checklist (schema-runway-checklist.xlsx) that breaks these down into owners and deliverables.

Proposed kickoff slots:
- Wed Apr 14, 10:00–11:00 PT
- Thu Apr 15, 14:00–15:00 PT

Owners on our side: Camila (implementation lead), Marissa (CS lead), Ben (commercial/POC terms).

If you want, loop in anyone from your infra or security team and I’ll add them to the invite.

Best,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Head of Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123
From: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@cardiotech.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Joanna Lee <joanna.lee@cardiotech.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Schema Gate: Implementation Runway & Preflight Checklist

Jonas —

Thanks, this looks useful. Wed Apr 14 at 10 PT works for us. I’ll bring our infra lead (Joanna) and a product engineer who owns the JSON contracts.

A couple initial notes from our side:
- We have a pre-existing JSON schema for report output; I will share the spec ahead of the call so we can map fields.
- Network team will want a short window to validate IP allowlist and proxy settings (likely a 48–72 hour lead).
- We prefer a conservative default for function timeouts: 5s for sync tool calls, 30s for async job kicks. Happy to discuss.

See you Wednesday.

Best,
Sophie

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Schema Gate: Implementation Runway & Preflight Checklist — kickoff notes and owners

Thanks for joining the call today — good alignment. Below are the action items and a compressed 3-week runway we agreed on. I attached the updated checklist (schema-runway-checklist.xlsx) with owners and acceptance criteria.

Summary of outcomes:
- Deliverable A: Canonical JSON schema v1.0 (CardioTech to provide existing schema by EOD Thu Apr 15). Acceptance: Redwood automated validator must return 0 schema errors on provided sample outputs. Owner: CardioTech (Sophie / Eng); Redwood (Camila) reviews.
- Deliverable B: Tool contract/IDL for function calls. Acceptance: Spec includes request/response examples, error codes, and a retry/backoff policy. Owner: Redwood (Marissa) + CardioTech (product engineer).
- Deliverable C: Streaming SLO profile & prefix caching config. Acceptance: P95 < 250ms for pilot traffic in dev environment; caching rules documented. Owner: Redwood (Camila)
- Deliverable D: Test harness & evaluation deck. Acceptance: Runbook with 50 sample prompts, evaluation matrix (precision + latency), and sample baseline results. Owner: CardioTech (Eng) + Redwood QA.
- Deliverable E: Security checklist / evidence handoff. Acceptance: basic SOC2 artifact & network allowlist confirmed. Owner: CardioTech security / Redwood security (Marissa)

Timeline (compressed):
- Week 0 (Apr 14–20): Schema handoff, network vetting, initial tool contract draft
- Week 1 (Apr 21–27): Integrate schema into validation pipeline; implement tool helpers; begin streaming config in staging
- Week 2 (Apr 28–May 4): Run test harness, fix regressions, produce evaluation deck, sign-off for limited pilot

Open action items (owners):
1) Sophie: upload CardioTech JSON schema and sample outputs (by 2027-04-15 EOD)
2) CardioTech infra: confirm IP allowlist window (target answer by 2027-04-16)
3) Marissa: share SOC2 evidence checklist and retention policy doc (by 2027-04-18)
4) Ben: prepare POC SOW addendum and draft start date (internal)
Attachments referenced: schema-runway-checklist.xlsx (updated with owners/criteria)
Notes on technical specifics we flagged during the call:
- Structured output: we recommend a top-level `records` array with each record including `id`, `type`, `timestamp`, and `payload` (payload is nested JSON that must follow provided schema). We’ll supply an automated validator script.
- Tool calling: prefer a single HTTP POST contract /tools/execute with body {name, args, call_id} and explicit `status` values on return. Redwood runtime will surface tool failures with error_code enum for deterministic handling.
- Streaming: set a soft token cap per response (e.g., 1,024) for the pilot and enable prefix/KV caching for repeated conversational prefixes to reduce cost.

I’ll sync with Marissa on the SOC2 artifacts and will loop legal if we need any specific DPA addendum.

Camila

--
Camila Reyes
Implementation Lead, Customer Solutions
camila.reyes@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Schema Gate: Implementation Runway & Preflight Checklist — commercial next steps

Sophie —

Quick note from the commercial side: to keep the timeline aligned with engineering I can draft the POC SOW addendum this week. Two asks from procurement we typically see:
1) Confirm expected monthly token/embedding forecast for the pilot (helps size Dedicated or host routing)
2) Any required NDA/contract redlines up front (we can provision a limited SOW while legal reviews redlines)

If you can provide an estimated token profile and a point of contact for procurement/legal, I’ll include those in the draft and share a DocuSign link for signatures.

I’ll also note internal kickoff milestones in the SOW: schema delivery, network sign-off, pilot start.

Thanks — Ben
--
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales

From: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@cardiotech.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Joanna Lee <joanna.lee@cardiotech.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Schema Gate: Implementation Runway & Preflight Checklist — confirming items

All —

Thanks for the plan and the checklist. Quick confirmations:
- Schema and sample outputs uploaded to the link you provided (we added v0.9 and historical samples).
- Network requirements attached (cardiotech-network-requirements.pdf) — infra flagged a couple of egress rules that need validation.
- Token profile: for the first 2 weeks of the pilot we expect ~250k tokens/week, mostly short streaming responses. We’ll add a conservative buffer in the SOW.
- On SOC2: we can provide the standard SOC2 summary report and a list of controls; Joanna will coordinate with Marissa for an evidence handoff next week.

Open question for Redwood: on tool retries, do you support idempotency tokens for function execution? We prefer at-least-once with an idempotency key.

If that’s acceptable I think we’re ready to move forward with the timeline — please send the SOW addendum when ready.

Best,
Sophie
